fixes.explanation: That's the word, baker. Moses says, “Do not test the LORD your God…” (Deuteronomy 6:16). He points back to a place Israel already knew, Massah. There the people tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?” (Exodus 17:7). I think Moses is telling them not to go down that road again.

Yep. Moses says, “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.” (Deuteronomy 6:9). Doorposts AND gates, baker. You know when you stick a note on the front door so you won't forget your keys? Same idea. The words go where your eyes will land.

Not guests, friend. Moses says, “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt (Exodus 6:11). That's where the answer to the son begins, and then it tells how the LORD brought them out.

problems.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
The passage does not say doorposts and gates cover every way in and out.
The oven joke compares trying not to notice a door with writing words as reminders. The actions do not match.
A mint on a pillow is a food reference outside the permitted exceptions.
The hotel-room joke makes light of slavery by contrasting it with a comfortable stay.
